item.title: Nvidia RTX Spark N1X processor arrives in high-end laptops
item.description:
Nvidia RTX Spark N1X processor arrives in high-end laptops

Nvidia’s RTX Spark N1X processor is finally here, and we’ve been testing a range of powerful laptops equipped with this new ‘superchip.’

🧩 Overview

Nvidia’s RTX Spark is designed as a high-performing Arm-based System on a Chip (SoC) for laptops and small desktop computers, positioning itself as a competitor to Apple, Intel, AMD, and Qualcomm. The chip features many CPU cores, Nvidia RTX Blackwell graphics, and unified memory capable of running sizable local AI models.

⚙️ Key details

  • The RTX Spark is exclusively available in high-end laptops
  • All tested models feature 20 CPU cores and 6,144 GPU CUDA cores in the flagship version
  • Lower cost configurations have 18 cores and 5,120 CUDA cores
  • Unified memory ranges from 32GB to 128GB across different models
  • Pricing starts at $2,599.99 for the 18-core version and goes up to $6,999.99 for the 20-core version

🚀 Availability

The RTX Spark is currently available in several premium laptops:

  • Microsoft Surface Laptop Ultra (128GB)
  • Asus ProArt P16 (both 64GB and 128GB configurations)
  • Lenovo Yoga 9n 2-in-1 (64GB)
  • HP OmniBook Ultra (32GB)

💡 Why it matters

The processor is aimed at developers, coders, and content creators who need the ability to run local AI models and utilize the latest gaming technologies like DLSS 5. Windows on Arm has improved significantly since previous generations, with native Arm apps working well and many x86 applications running through Microsoft’s Prism emulation layer.

Antonio Di Benedetto has made an RTX Spark his daily driver, running typical work and personal applications without issues. The chip handles daily tasks well but shows more variability in gaming performance.

Gaming performance

  • Black Myth: Wukong: 70fps at 3270 x 2180 with medium settings and DLSS
  • Cyberpunk 2077: 66fps with medium settings and DLSS
  • Forza Horizon 6: 57fps with medium settings and DLSS
  • Returnal: 60fps at 1440p with high settings
  • Jedi Survivor: 60fps with DLSS upscaled to 1200p and medium settings
  • Shadow of the Tomb Raider: 60fps at 1800p with highest settings

Performance varies significantly by game and settings, with some titles like Helldivers 2 and Star Wars Zero Company being more CPU-bound and showing lower frame rates.

#Nvidia #RTXSpark #AIcomputing #Armarchitecture #laptopprocessors

Source: A week with RTX Spark: everything we’ve learned using Nvidia’s new laptops

item.title: Sightlogix Launches NS12 and TC12 Megapixel Thermal Cameras for Large Scale Perimeter Security
item.description:
Sightlogix Launches NS12 and TC12 Megapixel Thermal Cameras for Large Scale Perimeter Security

Sightlogix has announced the Sightsensor NS12 and TC12, which are among the first fixed thermal cameras on the market to feature a 1280×1024 imager. These devices are designed to protect large sites and critical infrastructure perimeters using high-resolution thermal imaging and edge-based AI classification.

🔍 Overview

The higher resolution of the NS12 and TC12 allows each camera to protect approximately 2.5 times the area of a traditional 640×480 system. By increasing coverage per device, the system reduces the total infrastructure cost for wide-area sites.

  • Target Applications: Utility substations, data centres, airports, ports, and wide-area campuses.
  • Infrastructure Impact: Fewer cameras require fewer poles and fewer cable runs.
  • Detection Range: Both cameras deliver AI classification across the full inbound detection range.

🧩 How it works

The cameras are powered by the Sightlogix Gen7 edge processing platform, which includes a dedicated AI core. This platform delivers 20× the AI throughput of prior generations, providing the necessary processing headroom for megapixel thermal AI detection.

Feature Capability
Thermal Resolution 1280×1024 imager
AI Throughput 20× increase over previous generations
TC12 Dual-Stream Processes 1280×1024 thermal and 4K visible streams simultaneously
On-Device Validation Real-time cross-validation between streams with no cloud dependency

On the TC12 model, the Gen7 platform runs independent AI models on both the thermal and visible streams simultaneously to cross-validate detections entirely on-device.

💡 Why it matters

The system is engineered to address the specific scale of critical infrastructure. “Critical infrastructure perimeters don’t fit in a small box. The NS12 and TC12 were built for exactly that challenge — protecting more perimeter with fewer devices, with the AI classification performance and trusted alerts that operators can rely on,” commented Jim Hahn, CEO, Sightlogix. The company indicates these products are the result of more than 20 years of engineering for this application.

#Sightlogix #ThermalImaging #PerimeterSecurity #EdgeAI #ComputerVision

Source: Sightlogix introduces new family of thermal cameras

item.title: Congress Debates Legislative Solutions for Rising AI Data Center Electricity Costs
item.description:
Congress Debates Legislative Solutions for Rising AI Data Center Electricity Costs

Congress is scrambling to address voter concerns over the impact of AI data centers on residential electricity rates as lawmakers debate new legislative measures. With the data center industry rapidly expanding, regional utilities are building tens to hundreds of millions of dollars in new infrastructure, raising questions about how much of these costs will be passed on to everyday utility customers.

⚖️ Legislative Initiatives

Several data center and AI-related bills are moving through Congress. The primary competing measures include:

Bill Name Sponsor / Promoter Key Provisions & Status
Ratepayer Protection Act Sponsored by Ohio Republican Sen. Jon Husted Would have state utilities consider holding “large-load” customers responsible for increased costs. Passed the House in September with strong bipartisan support; opposed by Senate Minority Leader Sen. Chuck Schumer.
GRID Savings Act Authored by New Mexico Democrat Sen. Martin Heinrich; promoted by Sen. Chuck Schumer Aimed at protecting ratepayers; described by Schumer as having “more teeth” than the Ratepayer Protection Act because the Ratepayer Protection Act’s protections are voluntary.

⚙️ Rising Infrastructure and Utility Costs

The rapid growth of data centers has significantly impacted regional energy grids and wholesale electricity costs:

  • Overall Ratepayer Impact: PJM, a regional transmission organization serving 13 states and the District of Columbia (including Northern Virginia), has an Independent Market Monitor estimating that data centers have cost their 67 million ratepayers approximately $29 billion over roughly the past two years.
  • State-Level Costs: Maryland customers pay an estimated $168 to $216 more per year on electricity bills primarily due to the data center boom.
  • Infrastructure Demands: Utilities are constructing new power lines, substations, and other grid-connecting infrastructure. Connor Waldoch, co-founder and chief strategy officer at Grid Status, notes, “We’re talking tens to hundreds of millions of dollars [of infrastructure] that are being built by these local utilities.”
  • Cost Recovery: Jeremy L. Slayton, a spokesman for Dominion Energy, which serves Loudoun County, Virginia, stated, “We recover costs for distribution and transmission infrastructure from customers.”

🧩 Challenges in Determining Consumer Impact

Calculating the precise cost passed on to residential ratepayers is difficult due to several variables and a lack of transparency:

  • Local Variables: According to Lucy Qiu, a professor at the School of Public Policy at the University of Maryland, consumer impact depends on utilities’ power-purchasing contracts, retail rates, regulatory decisions, the scale of upgrades, and how utilities share accounting.
  • Lack of Transparency: Ari Peskoe, director of the Harvard Electricity Law Initiative, states that a “single, clean number” for nationwide data center costs is impossible because much of the data regarding what data centers pay is hidden behind non-disclosure agreements (NDAs).
  • Prevalence of NDAs: A study by the University of Mary Washington found that NDAs had been signed in 80% of Virginia localities where there were existing, approved, or proposed data centers.

💡 Political Ramifications

The issue of data center growth and energy costs has also entered political campaigns. Ohio Republican Sen. Jon Husted is currently in a heated reelection campaign against Democrat Sherrod Brown, who lost his Senate seat in 2024. Brown has made Husted’s past support of data centers in Ohio a major campaign issue.

#AIdatacenters #EnergyPolicy #RatepayerProtection #GridInfrastructure

Source: Data centers
